title: Apparently My Girlfriend Is a Murderer
author: Unknown

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.content:
Apparently My Girlfriend Is a Murderer Lights & Fire Tama doctor. One day, I come across a weird patient when I am on duty. The first thing she says when she sees me isn't that she feels unwell somewhere. Instead, she says something hair-raising. "Dr. Cantrell, your girlfriend is a murderer." "What nonsense are you spouting?" I shoot back with widened eyes and shoot up from my chair. I feel offended. She calmly says, "She won't be home tonight because she needs to deal with the body.

You will know whether what I say is true by tonight." Chapter 1 Beau's POV Ihada gentle and beautiful girlfriend. My friends envied me, and my family approved of her. I used to feel proud that she was mine. But all of that shattered in an instant because of the patient sitting in front of me. "Dr. Cantrell, your girlfriend is a murderer. She's going to kill you." "What nonsense are you talking about?" My eyes widened as I rose from the chair. I was deeply offended by what I had just heard.

"If you insult my partner again, I'll have security escort you out." My girlfriend, Kaylee Dishman, was gentle by nature. At work, she was approachable and well-liked by everyone. How could she possibly be a killer? The woman in front of me looked deathly pale, as though all the color had been drained from her face. She didn't seem the least bit surprised by my reaction. "You'll believe me eventually," she said. "You're a man of conscience." Her gaze slowly drifted to the plaque on my office wall. " Your girlfriend won't be coming home tomorrow night.

She's going to dispose of a body." After saying that, she got up and left. I frowned, convinced the woman was suffering from some kind of mental disorder. She should probably see a specialist. For the rest of the evening, I rested in my office. Since it wasn't the holiday season, the emergency department remained quiet throughout the night. It wasn't until morning that my coworker came to take over my shift. "Beau, did anything exciting happen last night?" he asked. "Twas on duty. What could possibly happen?" Marshall Covington looked surprised.

"You didn't forget Halloween was last night, did you?" I froze for a moment. Halloween? Wasn't it just another made-up holiday? "Dr. Covington, as a medical professional, I suggest you stick to scientific reasoning," I said, rolling my eyes at him. I gathered my things and stood up to leave. After getting home, I took a shower and immediately fell asleep on the bed. When I woke up again, it was already evening. I picked up my phone and sent Kaylee a message. "Kaylee, shall we have fried chicken tonight, just like always?" It was our little tradition.

When we first started dating, we were both broke students. For all four years of college, we always celebrated our anniversary with fried chicken. Today marked our anniversary once again. "T can't. Something came up at the office," she replied." You're on your own for dinner tonight. I'll be home late." Ilet out a soft "oh," a hint of disappointment settling in. Still, it didn't matter too much. Over the past two years, we had both become busy with work, and missing anniversaries wasn't unusual anymore. Iwas about to make myself a simple meal at home when my phone rang.

It was Kaylee's coworker and best friend, Winter Langley. "Beau, you two are seriously relationship goals," she said. "Kaylee even asked the boss for permission to leave work early today because it's your anniversary." Iwas taken aback as I read the message on my phone. Kaylee had clearly told me she was busy at work and couldn't come home tonight. But now, Winter said she had taken leave specifically to celebrate our anniversary with me. The stories didn't match. So, who was lying? Or was Kaylee secretly planning some kind of surprise for me?

With that thought, I didn't bother making dinner and simply waited in the living room for her surprise to arrive. One hour passed, then two, then three... By 10:00 pm, she still hadn't returned. Staring out at the dark, overcast sky, I took a deep breath. In the end, I never made the call. It was because I remembered what that woman had told me. "Your girlfriend won't be coming home tomorrow night. She's going to dispose of a body." a cP Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 2 Another 30 minutes passed, and Kaylee still hadn't returned. It was already past the latest time she would normally come home. I tried calling her, but I couldn't get through at all. Just as I was beginning to worry that something might have happened to her, she sent a message. "I'mina meeting at the office. I'll head back a bit later!" As I read it, my heart sank. Winter had already uploaded a video to social media of herself relaxing at home and watching TV-so how could Kaylee still be ina meeting at work? Something suddenly clicked in my mind.

Could that woman really have been telling the truth? I didn't think twice and drove straight to the hospital. I walked up to the nurses' station. The nurse on duty looked at me in surprise. "Dr. Cantrell, what are you doing here?" "Vanessa, pull up last night's patient records for me," I ordered, my face stiff and tense. Noticing my expression, Vanessa McKinnon didn't press for details and immediately went to handle it. "You were on duty last night, and only one patient came in. Here." With that, she handed me a printed medical record. 1 looked down at the name and phone number on it.

The woman was called Amber LeBlanc. I went back to my car and dialed her number. "Hello, Dr. Cantrell," she said, as if she had been expecting my call. "Where's Kaylee?" I asked. She let out a laugh. "I told you, didn't I? She's disposing of a body." I gritted my teeth. "Don't be ridiculous. Kaylee would never kill anyone." Amber paused for a moment. "So, you still don't believe me, huh? But I'll make sure you do." With that, the line went dead. I sat in the car, my mind in complete turmoil. When I got home again, Kaylee had already returned and was asleep.

Seeing her peaceful, almost childlike expression, I finally felt a sense of relief. No matter what, I would still choose to trust her. But just as I was about to drift off, [heard her murmur something in her sleep that sent a chill down my spine. "Amber..." The next morning came, and I woke up with dark circles under my eyes. Kaylee had already made breakfast and was waiting for me. "Kaylee, were you really working overtime at the office last night?" I asked, biting into the bread in my hand. It felt unusually dry today, and even the milk couldn't wash it down. She frowned.

"Of course, I was." "But your company has never stayed open that late," I said, faltering slightly. "Beau, what are you trying to say?" Kaylee suddenly raised her voice. "Are you really questioning me? What right do you have?" I couldn't understand why my usually gentle girlfriend had changed so suddenly. "That's not what Imeant-" "Enough. We should take some time apart. Beau, you're not who I thought you were." Kaylee kept her eyes fixed on me until she walked out the door. I knew we had fallen into a silent standoff. Her strange behavior left me completely confused.

I couldn't help but suspect that Amber was pulling the strings behind everything. Upon arriving at the hospital today, I found several police officers waiting in my office. "You must be Dr. Beau Cantrell." "Yes. What's this about?" "We've found that a woman named Amber LeBlanc came to see you two nights ago. Is that true?" the middle-aged officer asked, watching me closely. "Yes." I paused briefly. "She told me something strange. "What did she say?" "That someone would kill me. I can't make sense of it." Thesitated for a moment. In the end, I decided not to bring up Kaylee.

The officer's expression immediately turned serious. He handed me a death certificate with Amber's name and photograph. Cause of death: neuropathic pain.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.content:
Chapter 3 The officer said, "Amber has been dead for nine days." I froze. By the time I came back to my senses, the police had already left. My back was drenched in cold sweat. In hindsight, Amber's behavior that night didn't seem like that of a living person at all. For the rest of the day, I felt distracted and uneasy. Just as I was wrapping up my shift, Amber came looking for me again. "Hello, Dr. Cantrell," she said with a smile. "I'd like to have a check-up." Istared at her, my palms damp with sweat. There had to be a connection between her and Kaylee- perhaps they knew one another.

To get to the truth, I took her blood pressure and heart rate. Strangely, what the police had said didn't seem to be true. Amber appeared completely healthy, with no abnormalities in her vitals. "T don't know what your connection to Kaylee is, but she's a good person," I said. "I hope you won't hurt her." My words seemed to land heavily on Amber, and she stared at me in silence for along moment. Finally, she gave a faint smile. "Things aren't always what they seem. We'll meet again, Dr. Cantrell." With that, she walked away. Only then did I notice the goosebumps covering my skin.

As I was packing up to go home, I spotted an empty syringe on the floor. The wear on the needle made it obvious it had been used before. Still, the strange green liquid inside didn't match anything stocked in the emergency department. The moment I recognized the label on the syringe, every hair on my body stood on end. A cold wave surged from my feet to the top of my head. NECH nerve-blocking agent-this was a powerful drug with serious side effects, used specifically for treating neuropathic pain. Only one possibility remained-Amber was the one who had left it there.

The police officers came to see me. "Dr. Cantrell, we've reviewed the surveillance footage from the night you met Amber," the young officer said with a confused look. "It shows you were alone in your office the entire time. You never moved." "That's impossible." My eyes widened. I quickly brought out Amber's medical record from Halloween night, along with the used syringe. "After that night, Amber came to see me again. Oddly enough, I had deliberately checked her pulse and blood pressure, and everything was normal.

But she did leave this drug behind." The officer's expression tightened as he picked up the empty syringe. "What drug is this?" "NECH nerve-blocking agent. It's a medication used to treat neuropathic pain." The young officer watched me for a long moment. Finally, he said, "Thank you for your cooperation, Dr. Cantrell. We'll need to take this evidence back for further investigation. Is that alright?" I quickly nodded. "Of course." Imade my way home after leaving the hospital. As I opened the door, the smell of alcohol hit me. Neither Kaylee nor I drank, so where could it be coming from?

Seeing the high heels at the entrance, I knew Kaylee was in the bedroom. From the day things suddenly became strained between us, she hadn't spoken to me once. It felt as if we were no more than silent roommates, sharing a house while living completely separate lives. But while I was washing up in the bathroom, Kaylee suddenly appeared behind me. Her arms slid around my waist, pulling me close. "Beau, I'm so sorry about that day," she said softly. " Things at work have been rough recently, and it had affected my mood. It's all resolved now.

I hope you're not still mad at me." My heart skipped a beat. Whenever she uttered those words, it meant our silent standoff had come to an end. After drying my hands, I reached down and grasped her hands at my waist.

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.content:
Chapter 4. "Of course, I'm not mad at you. If work gets stressful next time, you can tell me. You don't have to carry it all by yourself." I turned around and looked Kaylee in the eyes. Her cheeks were tinged with a rosy flush. Standing so close, I could smell the alcohol on her breath. Iwas surprised. "Have you been drinking? I thought you never touched alcohol." Kaylee lowered her head slightly, resting it against my chest. Ina soft voice, she said, "I got everything at work settled, and I was just feeling happy tonight. Please forgive me, okay?

How about we go out for some barbecue?" She suddenly raised her head. Her eyes gleamed as they met mine. I was really tired, but since we'd just reconciled, I couldn't bring myself to spoil her good mood. "Sure." Kaylee couldn't wait any longer and tugged me out the door. Instead of driving like we normally did, she unexpectedly chose to walk with me. "Why are we walking? It's over half an hour away." My legs ached, and it felt like a heavy stone was pressing down on my back. Kaylee tilted her head up, smiled at me, and blinked her eyes.

"It's been a long time since we've taken a stroll like this. Just keep me company, okay? I'll give you a massage when we get home tonight." Inodded. Half an hour later, we finally arrived at the barbecue joint. Kaylee went to the restroom to touch up her makeup, leaving me sitting alone at a table by the street. My phone suddenly rang. Seeing the familiar number on the screen, I tapped the answer button. "Hello?" "Don't go home tonight. Your girlfriend is planning to kill you." "T don't care who you are or how you got my number. This isn't funny.

Don't ever call again." The voice on the other end was awoman's-one that sounded somewhat similar to Amber's. Panicked, I quickly hung up and tried to steady my breathing. Iordered the usual skewers that Kaylee and I liked, but as the dishes gradually came out, she still hadn't returned. "Sir, where is the restroom?" The owner of the barbecue joint pointed me toward one a few hundred yards away. I remembered Kaylee had walked in that same direction. Theaded toward the public restroom and pushed the door open. The men's restroom was on the left, and the women's was on the right.

In the middle of the corridor was a sink anda long rectangular mirror. Ilooked at my reflection and splashed water over my face. I had been staying up too much lately, and dark circles had formed under my eyes. Out of nowhere, I noticed a figure in the mirror- someone standing on the other side of the road. It was a woman. It looked like she knew I was watching her; she even raised her phone and waved it at me. That was when it struck me-she was the one who had just called. She then brought the phone to her ear. A second later, my phone rang. Sure enough, it was her. "Hey, Dr. Cantrell.

Would you like to head to your house with me right now?" I frowned at the woman across the street. After a brief hesitation, I gritted my teeth and made up my mind-I needed to deal with her immediately. I hung up the phone and called toward the restroom, " Kaylee, head back to the restaurant and wait for me. 1 need to take care of something. I'll be back soon!" With that, I walked toward the woman. The moment her face came into view, a wave of goosebumps swept over my entire body. "Amber?" She was dressed ina long black dress, her face completely drained of color. "Dr.

Cantrell, I'm glad you still remember me." Was she human or a ghost? Seeing her shadow on the ground, I felt somewhat relieved. "How do you know where I live?" I asked. What she said next, however, made my blood run cold. "Because I was at your place just a moment ago."

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.content:
Chapter 5 My face hardened. "If you keep talking nonsense and interfering with my life, I'll call the police." "Call them if you want. It won't make a difference." Hearing the word "police," Amber's tone stayed calm and indifferent. "If you saw the injuries on my body, I believe you'd come with me." She then lifted her dress in front of me. I instinctively looked away, yet I could still see blood dripping at her feet. As my gaze shifted upward, I noticed dense needle marks covering her legs. Her skin had turned a bluish- purple shade-the unmistakable sign of a severe drug overdose reaction.

There was also a deep cut on her thigh, exposing the bone beneath. Fresh blood continued to seep from the wound. Asa doctor, I was particularly sensitive to blood. "Are you out of your mind? Why haven't you gone to the hospital for a wound this serious?" Driven by medical duty, I tried to take her to the nearest clinic, but Amber pulled her hand away from mine. "Dr. Cantrell, you're a man of principle," she said, lowering her dress without a care. Her eyes stayed locked on my face. "These injuries were caused by your girlfriend. When you got home, she was in the bedroom tormenting me.

I would've died if you hadn't shown up. She even poured alcohol all over the house to mask the smell of blood." Her words sent a wave of horror through my mind. In hindsight, I realized Kaylee's behavior tonight had been far too abnormal. "T'll go with you, but only if I can see the evidence. I won't believe you without proof." "Thank you, Dr. Cantrell." Amber's gaze was filled with gratitude. Together, we headed back to my place. When I opened the door again, the smell of alcohol still lingered heavily in the air. "Sit down.

I'll treat your wounds first," I said, watching Amber's blood drip onto the floor. From what I knew as a doctor, a wound this severe could quickly lead to heavy blood loss and shock without immediate treatment. I reached into the drawer in the living room TV cabinet and pulled out a tourniquet, painkillers, and disinfectant. It was only then that I realized the couch was marked by a large damp patch, where the smell of alcohol hung strongest. Could Amber have been telling the truth? I had managed to temporarily control her bleeding, but I still couldn't perform proper stitches at home. "Dr.

Cantrell, take a look inside the bedroom. That's where the evidence is." Amber slowly got to her feet, steadying herself with her hands. I walked to the bedroom door and took a deep breath. As Topened it, a sea of red flooded my vision. The covers on the bed were drenched in blood. The bedroom reeked of alcohol more than anywhere else. Mixed with the stench of blood, it made my stomach churn violently. "Howis this possible?" My entire body tensed, cold sweat running down my back. I lifted the blanket.

On the bed lay several scattered syringes and a butcher's cleaver-the kind used in meat markets. Blood was smeared across its surface. At the same time, the floor was littered with more thana dozen empty alcohol bottles. Everything pointed to one conclusion-Amber had been telling the truth. The sight in front of me made my scalp crawl. I stumbled backward into the wardrobe. Amber caught me and guided me back to the couch in the living room. "Dr. Cantrell, would you like to hear my story?" Inodded quietly. She continued, "I'm Amber, and I have a sister named Isla.

We were born just ten minutes apart and look almost identical. "Two weeks ago, Isla went missing. I went to the police to report it, but all they found was her body. "According to the autopsy, she died in a car accident. However, the officer refused to let me see the body. What was even more bizarre was that my name appeared on her autopsy report. "That day, I felt like my world had collapsed. Once I got home, I went through Isla's belongings and founda contact named Q on her WhatsApp. When I opened the chat history, it was full of messages showing that Isla had been coerced by Q." a co?

Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.content:
Chapter 6 "From then on, I believed Isla's death was far more than amere car accident. I went back to the police station to file another report, only to be dismissed again by the same officer. He even confiscated Isla's phone." The more I listened, the more unsettled I became. "Why didn't you expose what happened?" "Because | later discovered that I was being watched as well. "What frightens me most is the possibility that the officer and the killer were in this together. They caused Isla's death.

I will make them pay for it." Amber's voice started to tremble, and tears spilled from her reddened eyes. "But the killer is still after me, and only now doI understand why she replaced Isla's name on the autopsy report with mine. "Because from the outset, I had always been her true target." My heart sank as I listened to her story. "You're saying Kaylee is the one who did it?" I asked solemnly. Amber slowly nodded. "Dr. Cantrell, you're the only one who can help me." "And what exactly do you expect me to do?" "Isla's death cannot be in vain.

From our two encounters, I can tell you're a good man. You wouldn't remain loyal to a murderer, would you?" I fell silent. Amber was right. Unless there was a rational explanation for what I had witnessed tonight, this unease would continue to haunt me. Since ancient times, one rule had always stood-an eye for an eye. Every debt must eventually be paid. "T understand. You should leave for now. I don't want Kaylee to become suspicious. I'll figure out what to do next." After sending Amber away, I shut the door and collapsed to the floor. My heart felt hollow.

Kaylee and I had shared a long, steady relationship that began in our student years. After all that time together, we had come to know each other deeply. I could never have imagined that the woman I had spent years of my life with could be such a ruthless, cold- hearted killer. I needed answers from her. In that instant, my phone rang. It was Kaylee. "Hello," answered, my voice rough and strained. "Honey, where did you go? I didn't see you at the barbecue joint." "Oh, something came up at the hospital. I've taken care of it.

I'm heading back now." There was a pause on the other end of the line. "Hello?" I said again. "Honey, I can't believe you'd lie to me over some woman. you don't even know." Suddenly, a loud knock rang out from the living room balcony. I whipped my head around, goosebumps spreading across my skin. Kaylee was already on the balcony-I never saw when she arrived. She had her face pressed against the soundproof glass, her features warped and nearly unrecognizable. Her eyes were bloodshot, veins fanning out like a spider's web.

"Why did you betray me?" With her hair falling loose, she slammed her fists against the glass door. Her voice sliced through the air like nails on a chalkboard. Seeing her in such a frenzied state, my eyes widened in terror. I retreated toward the security door, ready to escape at any moment. The woman standing before me was no longer the Kaylee I once knew. The glass door separating the balcony from the living room shook violently under her relentless blows. As attempted to flee and opened the door, a hand from outside grabbed me. "You can't go out.

The officer who confiscated Isla's phone is outside." Amber had come back, panic written all over her face. I looked past her, and sure enough, a dark figure was rapidly closing in. At that moment, only one thought echoed in my head: " It's over. Shut the door!" Asharp bang echoed through the air as I slammed the door shut. At once, heavy pounding erupted from outside the security door. Amber and I were trapped ina desperate situation. But deep down, I knew that only the evidence in the bedroom could save us.

chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.content:
Chapter 7 Seeing that I had locked the officer outside, Kaylee grew even more hysterical. She raked her nails across the glass door and even sank her teeth into it. "Let me out! All of you can go to hell! Fuck you, Beau!" Only then did I realize Kaylee had been trapped out on the balcony. Without a second thought, I pulled Amber into the bedroom and locked the door behind us. "We don't have much time. Hurry and find more evidence." Amber immediately began rummaging through the bedside table and the closet.

At the same time, I called the middle-aged officer who had come to see me the day after Halloween. He had given me his number. "Hello, this is Beau Cantrell. You came to my office the other day to ask about Amber's case. "Right now, we're trapped at home with the killer. My address is Unit 403, Building 3, Riverside Apartments!" There was no hesitation on the other end of the line. " I'm on my way." The call disconnected, but my heart was still pounding in my throat. The commotion outside the bedroom grew louder with each passing second. "Dr.

Cantrell, I found an old diary," Amber said, quickly handing it to me. With my back against the bedroom door, I opened it. The handwriting inside was Kaylee's, filled mostly with trivial memories from her time as a student. leven came across glimpses of our early days together, when our relationship had only just started. But soon, I noticed something strange. Kaylee's diary contained entries about another person. "Monday, May 19th: I met a man outside campus today. He said he knew Beau's former girlfriend. I was curious. What kind of woman could possibly deserve someone as good as Beau?

"That man handed me a USB drive filled with photos of Beau's ex-girlfriend. She was beautiful. My skin couldn't compare to hers, nor could my body. Even her name sounded better than mine... Isla." Abroken heart was drawn at the end of the entry. My heart sank. Who was this man who had suddenly appeared out of nowhere? I had never even known anyone named Isla. I kept reading. With each entry, Kaylee became increasingly obsessive. "May 23rd: I'm jealous of Isla. Why does she deserve so much of Beau's love?" "July 18th: That man showed up again today and gave me Isla's address.

I didn't even know she had a younger sister..." "September 17th: Q told me a story. If I were ever given the opportunity to kill her, I would first ensure I hada scapegoat..." The more I read, the more frightened I became. It felt as though my entire body had been plunged into an ice cellar. Qhad appeared. The same man who once coerced Isla had apparently been manipulating my relationship with Kaylee for years. The diary ended with a recent entry from ten days ago, containing just one line: "Qhas finally come to help me. I'll have what I want at last. Goodbye.

He is mine alone." Iclosed the diary, questions swirling in my mind. Kaylee seemed to have been molded into this obsessive version of herself by a man who had appeared from nowhere. 'That man was none other than Q. But what really made my blood run cold was the fact that Thad been targeted years in advance, all in preparation for the murder of a woman later on. The problem was, I didn't know Qatall. "What's in the diary?" Amber asked, her eyes fixed on my pale face. "Nothing much.

Someone named Q came up, but I'm not sure if it's the same man who coerced Isla." "Could he have coerced Kaylee as well?" Ishook my head. "No. He's spent years manipulating her into becoming a murderer." "That's messed up," she muttered under her breath. Without warning, the commotion outside the bedroom came toa halt. a oo Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.content:
Chapter 8 It was eerily quiet; only Amber's and my breathing could be heard. Amoment later, the security door seemed to swing open. Atush of footsteps flooded the living room, followed by the shouts of men. "Don't move! Police!" Inan instant, a scuffle erupted outside, but it was over just as quickly. Then came another knock-this time at the bedroom door. "Dr. Cantrell, the suspect has been apprehended. Please come out." After exchanging a glance with Amber, I went to open the door. The living room was packed with police.

Kaylee and another officer were on the floor, handcuffed and completely restrained. "It's you?" I recognized the officer pinned to the floor. It was the same young cop who had come to see me alone a few days earlier and taken the syringe from me. Wallace Gentry, the middle-aged officer, stepped forward and shook my hand. "Thank you, Dr. Cantrell. This man's badge number is fake. He's an impostor. "Also, everyone here will need to come with us tonight. We'll get to the truth after a proper interrogation." He pointed toward Amber behind me.

I said nothing and let them collect everything from the bedroom as evidence, though I kept the diary with me. Just before Kaylee was escorted into the police car, she looked back at me. The frantic, bloodshot look in her eyes had disappeared. She looked like her old self again, as if nothing had changed. But watching the police car pull away, I knew nothing would ever be the same again. There was no going back. Teventually requested a long leave of absence from the hospital. I sold my apartment and decided to travel elsewhere to clear my head.

It wasn't until I returned to the city that I learned the rest of what had happened. Wallace got in touch, and we arranged to meet up at a cafe. Injust half a month, he had become noticeably more worn and exhausted. "The case has been resolved. The young woman who had succumbed to neuropathic pain was Isla LeBlanc. She was the sister of the woman we escorted out of your apartment." Inodded; Amber had already told me about this. She had wanted to avenge Isla. "So, who exactly killed Isla?" "She ended her own life." Wallace paused, his gaze shifting to me.

"Or rather, you were responsible for her death." "Me?" I stiffened instantly, my eyes widening in shock. "A syringe used to treat neuropathic pain was found on. that fake officer, along with Isla's phone. The chat logs revealed her connection with him." "And what does that have to do with me?" "Let me finish," Wallace said, tapping his fingers lightly on the table. "That fake officer went by the online alias ' Q.' He admitted he met Isla through a niche fetish community. Have you heard of BDSM?" "A little," I replied with a nod.

"Qand Isla had a relationship like that-something close to a master-servant dynamic. Q confessed he had been psychologically controlling her for a long time. "Isla also suffered from a congenital nerve pain disorder and depended on regular injections to stay alive. On the day she died, Qconvinced her to lower her dosage, which triggered a severe mental breakdown. "She repeatedly resorted to self-harm-slashing her body, burning her skin with candles, and stabbing needles into her chest-all in a desperate attempt to ease the pain.

In the end, she tortured herself to death." I became even more confused. "So, why are you saying I'm responsible for her death?" Wallace picked up his cup and tooka sip. "Because Q. admitted that everything he did was driven by you. He wanted revenge." a fain Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.content:
Chapter 9 Q's POV My name was Rick Quiller, and I managed a factory workshop. I was working the night shift when my wife, Jessica Lowe, came in to confront me about my infidelity. Our argument quickly escalated and ultimately led toa fire breaking out in the workshop. Jessica suffered severe burns over most of her body and was left in critical condition, while I only sustained facial disfigurement. In that moment between life and death, I realized Jessica was still the person I cared about most. I carried her into the emergency room, where a bespectacled doctor was on duty.

He was gentle in his approach, and I trusted his medical expertise. Through tears, I begged him to save Jessica's life. He assured me that he would-but in the end, he failed. Jessica still departed anyway. Watching her body being wheeled into the morgue, every bit of regret and resentment hardened into hatred toward that doctor. Ifit weren't for him, my family might have survived. His name became permanently etched in my memory- Beau Cantrell. In the end, I spent all of our savings on reconstructive plastic surgery. I also resigned from my job at the factory.

I wanted to change my entire identity and get revenge on Beau. I wanted him to suffer the same pain of losing someone he loved. Through my investigation, I found that his girlfriend, Kaylee, also worked at the same company as my lover, Isla. Aplan slowly took shape in my head. I was determined to control Kaylee, reduce her to my plaything, and drive her to murder Beau with her own hands. Consequently, I had ordered Isla to spike Kaylee's meals with the NECH nerve-blocking agent on multiple occasions. Little by little, Kaylee's mind would fall further under my control.

Once she had been dealt with, the next step in my plan was to have her kill Beau. Things, however, quickly fell apart. After repeatedly lacing Kaylee's food with her own supply of the NECH nerve-blocking agent, Isla eventually ran out of it herself. After obtaining another dose of the medication, she died from an overdose while administering the injection. As it turned out, Isla had a younger sister named Amber.

To ensure Amber would never suspect me, I fabricated a story claiming that Isla had been Beau's first love, placing all suspicion on Kaylee-who was already nothing more than my puppet. To me, letting a fool like Amber die at Kaylee's hands wasn't a bad outcome. Ina single move, Kaylee would be labeled a cold-blooded murderer. Thad even manipulated Amber into staging an unnerving act right under Beau's nose, deepening his paranoia about Kaylee. Ultimately, my psychological trap would push them toward destroying each other.
